1.notes: Correct only for CRLF text files (Windows). On an LF file my clang run gave t=1,f=2 and garbage output; the claim's note and pitfall state the CRLF assumption.

4b.notes: Key b is right on all mainstream platforms (8==8 in my run) but the explanation 'all pointer sizes are equal' is not guaranteed by the C standard (implementation-defined; unmentioned).

4c.notes: ~0 is -1 on two's complement; other representations unmentioned (irrelevant in practice).

5.notes: 408 is the 32-bit answer, 416 on 64-bit (clang run). Official text says sizeof has type int (it is size_t) and printf %d with size_t is UB; claim's transcriber note covers the 4/8 split.
